newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. county to appeal $1 bn LILCO refund.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. county to appeal $1 bn LILCO refund.

text.p: The Suffolk County government said Friday it plans to appeal a Thursday state court ruling that grants the Long Island Lighting Co (LILCO) as much as $1.16 billion in refunds and interest for overtaxing its mothballed Shoreham nuclear power plant.
"We have the right to appeal," said Rick Belyea, press secretary for Suffolk County's executive office.
"You're looking at a matter of days and weeks," he said, when asked when the appeal likely would be filed.
He said the county's attorney began studying the 206-page decision. "We have a lot work to do," he said.

LILCO recently was awarded a $81 million refund for excess property taxes on its Shoreham nuclear power station while it was under construction. LILCO dropped out of the project in 1989 and decommissioning began in 1992.
"The judge has ruled that Brookhaven Town has grossly overassessed this property (Shoreham)," LILCO vice-president of external affairs Joseph McDonnell said in a statement.

"These payments significantly increased the costs of the Shoreham project and the cost of electricity on Long Island. Exclusive of litigation costs, we have pledged that all of these refunds will be used to ease the electric rate burden of our customers," McDonnell continued.
LILCO said it paid $542.6 million in taxes for Shoreham from 1984 to 1992 and $261.7 million for pilot payements from 1992 to 1996.
"We stand to get money back depending on how it gets through the courts," said Dave Viser, spokesman for Nassau County's executive office. Nassau, bordering Suffolk County, is also served by LILCO.

LILCO customers pay some of the country's highest electricity rates, which were driven up by huge costs linked to closing and decommissioning Shoreham. The plant was shut due to environmental concerns before ever starting production.
"We want to be sure Nassau County customers are properly reimbursed for LILCO's overcharges for Shoreham," he added.
The decision, if upheld, could financially devastate Suffolk County, Brookhaven Town and the Shoreham-Wading school district.
New York Governor George Pataki and the Long Island Power Authority (LIPA) have earlier said they would seek to cushion any adverse impact if the refund is implemented.
"There'll be protection for Suffolk County taxpayers. There's no immediate tax increase in the horizon," Belyea said, but declined to give specifics about the safety net.
"We're looking at what LIPA's doing," he said.
LIPA has has been evaluating restructure plans for LILCO, including a possible state takeover of the utility.
Justice Thomas Stark of New York's state supreme court in Riverhead, L.I., reportedly ruled in favor of a refund for LILCO due to flawed method in tax assessment for Shoreham.
